correctness.rationale: Either coordinate equality of squares forces w=−z (z≠0). Since the Möbius automorphism is injective and cannot have both b_a(z)=b_a(−z)=0 for a>0, equality of cubed values requires their quotient to be ω or ω². The resulting two quadratics z²±i c_a z−1=0, c_a=(1−a²)/(sqrt3 a), are interchanged by z↦−z. For c>2 only the small imaginary root lies in the disc; c=2 double unit root; c<2 two different unit roots. c=2 uniquely yields a=2−sqrt3. Derivatives vanish at z=0 and z=a respectively, never together. The exact Badea Thm7.3 injectivity-plus-unramified characterization makes collision failure sufficient. Recomputed representative roots and Möbius-cube equalities independently, with no finite sampling used as global proof.
